title: Sets: HashSet
summary: A collection with no repeats, and how to pick a list, a set or a map.

say.never: Think of a sticker collection. Getting the same sticker twice doesn't make your collection bigger. A **HashSet** works the same way: adding something that's already in it changes nothing. `contains` asks "is it in there?" and gets an answer fast, even with thousands of items. A set doesn't keep any order.
say.bit: A **HashSet** ignores repeats. `contains` is fast; there's no order.

steps.title: In your lesson: No repeats allowed

say.never: Scouts write down the same team many times, once per match. `TeamsSeen` keeps the team numbers in a `HashSet<Integer>`, so each team counts once. Import `java.util.HashSet`, add the `teams_` field, and each method is one line: `add`, `contains` and `size()`.

Picking the right collection makes the code short. Ask one question. Does the **order** matter, or can the same thing appear **twice**? Use a list. Do you only care **whether** something is there? Use a set. Do you **look things up** by a key, like a name or a number? Use a map, which is the next guide.
say.bit: Order or repeats: list. Is it there?: set. Look up by key: map.

board.code:
ArrayList  -> lap times, in order
HashSet    -> which badges I've earned
HashMap    -> phone book: name -> number
